referenceReview.boundary: PlayFlow, Nakama, Firebase, and Supabase remain reference-only, with no reference API, source, dependency, or wire contract copied. Agones is no longer reference-only: its client loop shape (sdks/csharp/sdk/AgonesSDK.cs and sdks/unity/AgonesSdk.cs at v1.60.0, commit 67b44a783218f7811084adaa5d9b334fb28e44ba) is adopted under Apache-2.0 as a marked modified derivative in Yogabase.Yogabase.RuntimeHost and its Unity package, retargeted to Yogabase's own self-scoped runtime-host routes. No Agones name, proto/sdk wire contract, resource concept, or host-port policy was adopted. The unmodified licence ships at licenses/Apache-2.0-Agones.txt; the full copying boundary is recorded in docs/REFERENCE_REVIEW.md

contract.mirroredFrom: Byte-identical, like the builds, delivery and runtime-host documents below, to the product's published documents as of 2026-10-08; this document (SHA-256 5fcbed400575ae191a577202a3548e41f7ef1b18f90971d7b58fc2e71fa867de) last changed on 2026-10-08, the delivery document (SHA-256 d44f95c0364d49071aa29e0d555687c942d91acbc9215cb71bd1eefb294d9c39) on 2026-10-03, the builds document (SHA-256 368a15e2baa2567983894752444cf7efe5687da2e40b461cef7523d124923750) on 2026-09-22 and the runtime-host document (SHA-256 c09a0842c3e295685a4112638ea74a6ab23e3b390fe2f6ab0e1a635f1e6797e2) on 2026-09-17, and all four were compared byte for byte with the product's published files on 2026-10-08. It carries the player-facing /v1/servers/* game-server surface, the three external sign-in routes for a project's end users (/auth/external/{provider}/start, /return and /callback, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08; the callback now requires the codeVerifier whose challenge start received), the requested-only realtime-presence and data-rest capability rows with the X-Yogabase-Accept-Capabilities request header, the restored client Data API (/v1/data/{table}/select|insert|upsert|update|delete, 2026-09-23) with its named 413 data_request_too_large, the storage refusal codes (2026-09-24), the inline payload limit with the 413 payload_too_large refusal on the function invoke route (2026-10-03) and on the actor invoke, workflow start and workflow cancel routes at 480 KiB (x-yogabase-orleans-payload), the durable Jobs routes (/v1/projects/{projectId}/jobs, 2026-10-03, x-yogabase-jobs) and the schedule routes (/v1/projects/{projectId}/schedules/{scheduleId} and its /trigger, 2026-10-03, x-yogabase-schedules), which three later product changes of the same day tightened: a manual run of a schedule whose function version is no longer admitted is a 409 where it was a 503, and both policies are required; a write holds scheduleId to one rule, the pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._~:-]{0,127}$; and the concurrency policies state what the scheduler does about an earlier occurrence that has not finished. The mirrored document (SHA-256 5fcbed400575ae191a577202a3548e41f7ef1b18f90971d7b58fc2e71fa867de) declares all of the above; the product commits that made these changes are not named here. Kiota therefore generates request builders for the Jobs and schedule routes in TypeScript, Python, Java and Dart, and the authored Jobs and schedule clients sit beside them (jobsSurface and schedulesSurface below).

schedulesSurface.preconditions: A create sends If-None-Match: * (201), an update sends If-Match with the ETag last read (200), and a delete (204) and a manual run (POST .../trigger, 202) send If-Match; a stale or unmet precondition is 412, a missing one 428, and both at once or a malformed ETag 400.
schedulesSurface.eTag: "schedule-v<version>-<instance as 32 lowercase hex>"; the version is decimal text, a 64-bit number a JSON number cannot carry, that the scheduler also advances as it runs, so an ETag held for long is stale. Every client reads it from the response header and checks it against the body, except Dart, whose typed send cannot read headers and derives it from the body.
schedulesSurface.namedRefusal: 413 schedule_payload_too_large (limitBytes 1,048,576 and maxBodyBytes 8,394,167); every other refusal is a status with a fixed title and no code, or no body, which the clients name by status (precondition_failed, precondition_required, not_found, conflict, forbidden, unsupported_media_type, request_failed).
schedulesSurface.knownGatewayLimits: None is recorded against the contract as tightened on 2026-10-03 (declared in the mirrored document, SHA-256 5fcbed400575ae191a577202a3548e41f7ef1b18f90971d7b58fc2e71fa867de). A product build from before the three commits of 2026-10-03 behaves as the earlier contract said: the scheduler stores concurrencyPolicy but starts every occurrence whichever is chosen, a manual run of a schedule whose function version is no longer admitted answers 503, a schedule id that contains a slash cannot be written (400) and any other id of 1 to 128 trimmed characters is accepted. The clients follow the later contract; the end-to-end evidence below was taken against the earlier build and was not repeated against the tightened contract.

buildsContract.notGeneratedReason: A developer-tool surface (Unity Editor, CLI, CI) reached with a project-scoped ybt_ developer token, not a shipped-client surface. The .NET YogabaseBuildsClient and the Unity package implement it by hand, including the Lambda execution declaration and registeredLambdaIds; no other language needs a client for it yet, so none is generated.

runtimeHostContract.notGeneratedReason: The document declares instance-addressed paths (/instances/{instanceId}/...), but a hosted workload calls the self-scoped relay routes /runtime-host/v1/self/{heartbeat,ready,reserve,shutdown,assignments} and never learns or asserts its own instance id. Generating from this document would emit the wrong surface for a workload, so it is checked in and checksum-verified as the server-side reference for lifecycle states and error codes only; the workload module is hand-authored.

runtimeHostSelfContract.mirroredFrom: A byte-identical copy of the product's published document of the same name, taken on 2026-10-20 (SHA-256 a2a9e201eaee833251f66eb89acc73edd7ce06383170824d39f6b386509f95aa). It describes the self-scoped loopback relay a hosted workload calls: POST heartbeat, ready, reserve and shutdown and GET assignments under /runtime-host/v1/self/, the lease and page schemas (including headState and headSequence), each route's refusal codes, the relay's own limits (a 64 KiB request body, 64 pending calls, a 30 second answer timeout, 100 events per page, reservations clamped to 1 to 600 seconds, a 30 second lease, a 300 second drain window and a 2 second retry hint) and the three statuses the relay answers with no body (413, 429 and 504), in its top-level x-yogabase-runtime-host-relay extension.
runtimeHostSelfContract.notGeneratedReason: The authored runtime-host client (src/dotnet/Yogabase.Yogabase.RuntimeHost, and the Unity package under languages/unity/io.yogabase.runtime-host) speaks these five routes by hand, with its heartbeat loop, its wait-out of RUNTIME_HOST_INSTANCE_PENDING and its resume-token polling, and no other language has a runtime-host client. The document is checked in and checksum-verified; nothing is generated from it.
